models_evaluated: DERM (Deep Ensemble for Recognition of Malignancy)

links.outcome: Cancers missed among lesions AI deemed benign that would be discharged without human review
links.effect: In lesions the AI deemed benign and that would have been discharged with no human review, four cancers were diagnosed.
links.quote: In lesions that the AI deemed benign, and that would have been discharged with no human review, four cancers were diagnosed.

links.outcome: AI diagnostic accuracy of exact diagnosis and lesion type versus dermatologists
links.effect: AI correct precise diagnosis 28.6% vs dermatologists 61.6% (P<0.001); correct tumour/lesion type 51.4% vs 75.5% (P<0.001); PPV 46.5% vs 62.1%.
links.quote: AI correctly identified the precise diagnosis 28.6% of the time, compared with dermatologists 61.6% of the time (P < 0.001).

screen.reason: Prospective real-world deployment study of an AI skin cancer screening algorithm (DERM) in an NHS clinical pathway, evaluating diagnostic accuracy and specifically analyzing safety implications of human review versus autonomous discharge without human review.
